narrative:
The model estimated a 72% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt. Because that risk is high, your law school application was denied; this is a forecast, not a judgment that you cannot succeed.

Among the factors that most affected this forecast, undergraduate GPA carried the greatest weight. Your 2.60 GPA is below the 3.23 average of accepted students, and it pushed the decision toward failure. Your family-income bracket was the second most influential factor and also pushed toward failure; although upper-middle income is common among accepted students, in your profile it added risk. Third was your first-year class decile: at 7, above the accepted average of 6.00, it also moved the forecast toward failure. Together these factors outweighed signs in your favor, such as an LSAT above the accepted average.

To move forward, ask admissions for specific feedback, consider additional coursework or a graduate credential to strengthen your academic record, prepare for a possible LSAT retake if it can improve your profile, and include a concise addendum explaining your GPA context. Reapply when you can show stronger evidence of bar-exam readiness, and choose schools where your profile is a better fit.
